No second full deadline extension has been announced post-Oct 31 2026, so level 2 is not met; deadlines were moved from original dates, so level 0 is excluded.

license_flow.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 (April 4, 2025) case-by-case export licensing on seven medium/heavy rare earths (Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y) and derivative magnets remains fully in force and was never suspended; processing times run 45 days to several months with no statutory deadline. Separately, MOFCOM Announcement No. 58 of 2026 (issued Nov 9, 2026) extends the suspension of Oct-2025 Announcements 55-58, 61, and 62 until January 10, 2027. Sources: SMM/Reuters (Nov 9 2026); carraglobe.com (Oct 2026); rare-earth-mining.com.
license_flow.rationale: The core April 2025 regime imposes case-by-case licensing with processing times routinely exceeding 45 days on named magnet categories — squarely within rubric level 1 (SLOWING). The Oct-2025 expansion remains suspended (extended to Jan 10, 2027 today), so no new categorical denial has been added, precluding level 2; but the persistent case-by-case burden and multi-month processing times preclude level 0.

truce_status.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 58 of 2026 (issued ~Nov 7-9, 2026) formally extends six rare-earth export-control suspensions from Nov 11, 2026 to Jan 10, 2027; BIS filed a Federal Register rule (Nov 5, effective Nov 9) extending the Affiliates Rule suspension to the same date. genius_impl.fact: As of November 9, 2026 (Gibson Dunn client alert, same date), the OCC is the only primary federal payment stablecoin regulator to have finalized its GENIUS Act rules (OCC final rule issued Oct 21, 2026; FR doc 2026-21706; effective Jan 18, 2027). The Federal Reserve remains at the NPRM stage (two NPRMs published Sept 24/29, 2026; comments due Nov 30, 2026). The FDIC NPRM (Apr 7, 2026; comments closed Jun 9, 2026) is not finalized. The statutory rulemaking deadline of July 18, 2026 was missed by seven federal agencies. Inter-agency divergence is documented: the Fed proposes a standardized risk-based capital framework vs. OCC's individualized approach; the FDIC requires segregated reserve pools per brand vs. OCC's case-by-case evaluation. Source: Gibson Dunn, 'The GENIUS Act: OCC Finalizes Its Payment Stablecoin Framework,' Nov 9, 2026; OCC News Release 2026-92; Yahoo Finance / stablecoininsider.org.
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric scores 1 (GAPS) when rules remain in proposed/comment stage near the deadline OR documented inter-agency divergence exists. Both conditions are met: the July 18 statutory deadline was missed by most agencies, the Fed and FDIC have not finalized rules (Fed comments close Nov 30), and material inter-agency divergence on capital and reserve-pool requirements is documented. No court stay or compliance-failure event elevates this to 2.

govt_stability.fact: France's National Assembly unanimously rejected the government's 2027 budget (all 458 participating lawmakers voted against) on 4 November 2026 (CNBC/Politico Europe, 5 Nov 2026). Lecornu's minority government remains in office; no no-confidence motion has yet been filed or passed over the 2027 budget. The government is expected to invoke Article 49.3 again, with the budget sent to the Senate from 20 November.
govt_stability.rationale: Lecornu governs without a majority, relies on Article 49.3 to pass budgets, and has survived all prior no-confidence votes. The unanimous rejection of the 2027 budget on 4 Nov 2026 deepens fragility but does not constitute a collapse: no confidence vote was passed and the PM has not resigned or dissolved parliament. This squarely fits rubric band 1 (FRAGILE).
govt_stability.change_reason: new_event: National Assembly unanimously rejected the 2027 budget on 4 November 2026, confirming and deepening the fragile minority dynamic — but no government collapse has occurred, so value remains 1.

pension_leverage_event.rationale: No regulator has flagged LDI liquidity stress and no forced gilt selling or BoE intervention has occurred in 2026; the slow, broad-based yield rise since end-2025 (0.91 pp over ~9 months in the UK) is structurally incapable of triggering the doom-spiral dynamics of 2022, confirming rubric band 0 (NONE).

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman PPFI funded ratio dips to 87.4% after -1.4% monthly return: PPFI asset value declined from $6.162 trillion to $6.067 trillion while total pension liability swelled to $6.944 trillion as of September 30, 2026. Source: Milliman PPFI release via Business Wire / financialcontent.com, published October 28, 2026. https://www.financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-10-28-milliman-analysis-september-market-losses-erase-112-billion-in-funded-status-for-public-pensions
funded_ratio.rationale: The most recent Milliman PPFI public-pension update (published October 28, 2026) reports 87.4% funded as of September 30, 2026; no subsequent PPFI public-pension release for October 31 has appeared as of November 9, 2026, so the prior reading is unchanged. The rubric calls for a representative large US public-pension funded ratio, which the Milliman 100 PPFI directly supplies.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (data workbook May 2026, PDF June 2026, emp.lbl.gov/queues): 'The median project built in 2025 took 61 months from the interconnection request to commercial operations' — down from 63 months for the 2024 in-service cohort.
interconnection_months.rationale: The authoritative LBNL source directly states 61 months for the 2025 in-service cohort, which is the rubric's target metric; this is confirmed by multiple corroborating secondary sources and no newer LBNL edition exists as of 2026-11-09.

dc_moratoria.fact: electricchoice.com (updated ~Nov 6, 2026): '583 data center restrictions active across 46 states'; NY EO 62 (statewide moratorium, signed Jul 14, 2026) confirmed still in force with no fixed end date; SAVRN tracker (Nov 3, 2026) logs 1,299 local jurisdiction actions; additional statewide-scope actions in TX (Gov. directive pausing grid connections/permits, Aug 3), OR (state-land pause through Jul 1 2027), and OK (moratorium enacted Sep 29, 2026).
dc_moratoria.rationale: Rubric band 2 requires a confirmed statewide moratorium OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses. NY's EO 62 alone satisfies the statewide threshold; 583 enacted restrictions across 46 states far exceeds the >10 local threshold. No new development since Oct 27 changes the band.

dissent.view: Quorum (Oct 2026) states NY is the ONLY state with a statewide moratorium and that no state has enacted one by statute; DWT law blog notes EO 62 is not a blanket construction ban but only pauses discretionary DEC environmental permits for 50 MW+ facilities — characterising it as narrower than headlines suggest.

theaiconsultingnetwork.com (corrected Sep 22, 2026) previously misreported Maine as having enacted a statewide moratorium; Maine's LD 307 was vetoed Apr 24, 2026 and no statewide moratorium took effect there.

ai_power_pressure.fact: ERCOT energization pause for data centers and crypto facilities ≥75 MW, ordered Aug 3 2026 by Gov. Abbott directing PUCT/ERCOT to audit all ~474 GW of queue entries before any project advances, remains active as of Nov 5 2026 (ERCOT Community Impact RFI PUC Update, Nov 5 2026, confirming 433/465 loads ~177 GW under RFI, Batch Zero reports due Dec 10 2026). PUCT Docket 59220 (Jul 24 2026) separately imposed a confirmed 525.5 MW emergency curtailment obligation on two co-located data centers (PUCT/White & Case, Jul 2026).
ai_power_pressure.rationale: The ERCOT energization pause is a power-scarcity-driven moratorium on new data center grid connections — the rubric-2 condition of 'a power-scarcity-driven moratorium' — still in force as of Nov 5 2026. PUCT Docket 59220 confirms an actual curtailment obligation imposed on operating data centers, satisfying the rubric-2 requirement for 'confirmed curtailment of data-center load.' [reversal guard: 1 -> 2 would undo the change made on 2026-11-02; held at 1 until a second consecutive read confirms it]
ai_power_pressure.change_reason: new_event: ERCOT energization pause for data centers ≥75 MW (Gov. Abbott order Aug 3 2026, confirmed still active via ERCOT Community Impact RFI PUC Update Nov 5 2026) and PUCT Docket 59220 (Jul 24 2026) imposing 525.5 MW curtailment obligation on co-located data centers — both constitute power-scarcity-driven moratorium/confirmed curtailment meeting rubric level 2, not fully weighted in prior reading which focused on PJM/DOE order expiry

dissent.view: PJM: no confirmed forced curtailment of data centers; DOE Order 202-26-50 expired without EEA-3 or customer impacts per PJM statement; FERC rejected IRAS curtailment framework Oct 9/12 2026 — PJM conditions alone would remain level 1

NERC (May 2026) reduced ERCOT summer demand forecast by 3.7 GW precisely because more data centers CAN be curtailed when needed — framing curtailment capability as a reliability improvement, not an emergency in force

mine_disruptions.fact: Grasberg Block Cave operating at ~67% of normal capacity through end-2026, with PTFI producing 249 Mlb copper in first 9 months of 2026 (Tony Wenas, PTFI President, Minerba Convention Jakarta, Nov 3 2026); Kamoa-Kakula full-year 2026 output now expected at ~290,000 t vs ~500,000 t design capacity (Ivanhoe Q3 2026 earnings release, Nov 3 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Two top-20 copper mines - Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula - have confirmed, currently active production cuts running well below design capacity, with combined lost output of ~400,000-470,000 t in 2026 versus normal; multiple institutions (Goldman, Citi, JP Morgan, ICSG) have published copper market deficit forecasts for 2026, satisfying the CLUSTER criterion (>=3 mines OR deficit forecast). Escondida's threatened strike was averted Oct 16 2026, so no new third mine disruption was confirmed; the two ongoing disruptions alone with institutional deficit forecasts are sufficient for the rubric's band-2 qualifier.

dissent.view: Escondida strike risk (Oct 2026) could have added a third major mine disruption, but BHP and union reached agreement on Oct 16 2026, averting any confirmed output cut at the world's largest copper mine

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG October 2026 biannual forecast (issued 14-15 Oct 2026): global refined copper market surplus of ~104,000 metric tons in 2026, widening to ~368,000 mt in 2027. Source: Mining Weekly (15 Oct 2026): 'The International Copper Study Group forecast on Wednesday that the global refined copper market would remain in surplus through 2027, with it widening from about 104 000 metric tons in 2026 to 368 000 metric tons in 2027.'
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: ICSG officially forecasts a +104,000 mt refined copper surplus for 2026 — well above the +100kt threshold for the SURPLUS band (score 0). No post-Oct-15 ICSG revision or new physical data has emerged to alter this classification.

dissent.view: April 2026 ICSG forecast cited a 96,000 mt surplus for 2026 (vs. October 2026's 104,000 mt) — both are surplus readings, so rubric outcome is identical; some secondary sources (discoveryalert.com, recyclingtoday.com) still reference the April figure.

drought_chip_farm.fact: USDM National Drought Summary (droughtmonitor.unl.edu, data valid Nov 3 2026, released Nov 5 2026): 'short-term drought has ended for the Southwest and Great Basin' following broad 1-category improvement; Taiwan WRA (wra.gov.tw, Oct 31 2026): Shimen 100%, Te-Chi 98.05%, Sun-Moon-Lake 96.84%, Tsengwen 88.06%, Wu-Shan-Tou 87.06% — all near or above normal, no rationing order in force.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: Short-term drought in the US Southwest has ended per the Nov 5 USDM release; only residual long-term drought persists in scattered non-core areas, none at D2+ in named chip/farm hubs. Taiwan reservoirs are at or near normal with no rationing order, so neither the D2 threshold nor any rationing criterion for value=1 is met.
drought_chip_farm.change_reason: new_event: USDM (Nov 5 2026, data valid Nov 3 2026) confirmed short-term drought ended for the Southwest and Great Basin, eliminating the D2 conditions that anchored the prior value=1 reading.

dissent.view: Lingering long-term drought remains in parts of the Southwest (northern Nevada, NW Utah, N Colorado per NIFC Nov 2026 outlook), which could arguably sustain D1-D2 in limited sub-areas — but no confirmed D2+ in the core farming/fab hubs (AZ, CA Central Valley, NM).

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,039.55 ft, storage 6,946,730 acre-feet, 26.6% of USBR active capacity (26,120,000 AF basis) as of Nov 7, 2026 — an all-time record low; minimum power pool is 950 ft, reservoir ~89.5 ft above that threshold. Source: USBR RISE API via coloradorivermonitor.com and westwaterwatch.com (Nov 7, 2026).
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.6% of active capacity, Lake Mead is unambiguously below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold. The reservoir remains at an all-time record-low elevation, confirming the CRITICAL classification is still fully in force.

dissent.view: lakelevelstoday.com reports 'Percent of pool: 43.3%' for Nov 7, 2026 — this appears to use full gross capacity (28.23M AF) rather than USBR active/available capacity (26.12M AF), yielding a materially different percentage; on the active-capacity basis used by USBR for shortage declarations the figure is 26.6%.

water_dispute.fact: Pakistan Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gillani, at Pakistan Water Week in Islamabad on 2 Nov 2026, declared any attempt to block or divert Pakistan's water share 'will be treated as an act of war,' reaffirming PM Shehbaz Sharif's identical formulation of 21 Oct 2026; India's IWT abeyance remains in force and India has rejected the PCA's 31 Aug 2026 ruling that the treaty is fully binding (Al Jazeera, 1 Sep 2026; ISAS NUS, 17 Aug 2026; Dawn, 1 Nov 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: The IWT suspension is a standing treaty abeyance (Level 1 floor) and the Senate Chairman's explicit 'act of war' threat on 2 Nov 2026 — within the 90-day window — satisfies the rubric's Level 2 criterion for an explicit war threat tied to a river/dam by a senior government official. No new post-2 Nov 2026 event alters the classification.

dissent.view: Some analysts (e.g. globaldefensecorp.com, 9 Nov 2026) characterise the water-war rhetoric as 'mostly rhetorical' and argue India's existing infrastructure cannot yet physically shut off Pakistan's water, suggesting the dispute is a 'strategic securitisation' rather than an imminent armed conflict — implying a Level 1 reading.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October 2026, down 1.6 points (1.2%) MoM from revised September level, but still 5.9% above year-earlier level. Source: FAO (fao.org/newsroom/detail/fao-food-price-index-edges-down-in-october-amid-subdued-demand/en), released 6 November 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM decline of 1.2% ends the three-month rising streak, so the rubric 2 (SPIKING) threshold is not met; however, the index remains 5.9% above year-ago levels and the MoM move is well within the <3% band, keeping it in the ELEVATED (1) category since the YoY increase prevents classification as FALLING (0), which requires both MoM and YoY declines.
fao_food_trend.change_reason: new_event: October 2026 FFPI published 2026-11-06 at 133.9 points (-1.2% MoM, +5.9% YoY); index pulled back from September peak but YoY remains firmly positive, sustaining the ELEVATED band rather than triggering a downgrade to FALLING.

china_export_curbs.fact: Diamondinterchem.com (citing trade sources, Nov 3 2026) reports 'China Phosphate Rock Export Quota Suspension Extends to 2027'; Oilchem/China General Administration of Customs data for Jan-Sep 2026 shows DAP exports of 73,900 t and MAP of 112,600 t (~95% below 2025), with September recording zero DAP and zero agricultural MAP shipments; Argus (cited by Prosperous America, ~Nov 5 2026) now forecasts phosphate export restart only in May 2027, confirming the post-Aug-31 suspension is extended well beyond its original deadline.
china_export_curbs.rationale: The original phosphate suspension (NDRC, Dec 2025, through Aug 31 2026) has been extended with no official reopening guidance issued; a Nov 3 2026 source confirms the quota suspension now extends to 2027 — a new broadening of the restriction within the trailing 3 months that moves the rubric from IN PLACE (1) to TIGHTENED (2). Urea quota remains in force but phosphate is the load-bearing product given the near-total export collapse and the confirmed extension.
china_export_curbs.change_reason: new_event: China phosphate rock export quota suspension formally extended to 2027 (diamondinterchem.com, Nov 3 2026); Argus forecasts no phosphate restart until May 2027, confirming the post-Oct-19 extension of the phosphate ban beyond its original Aug 31 2026 end-date into a new, longer suspension window.

dissent.view: Fertiaxis/MOFCOM (Oct 2026) notes the 3.3Mt 'urea quota' is actually an import tariff-rate quota, not an export ceiling — meaning urea self-discipline arrangements are less formally binding than commonly reported; September urea exports hit a record 2.45Mt, suggesting urea side is effectively open under self-discipline, arguing against full 'tightening' on nitrogen.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 1 commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz on November 1, 2026 — its most recently published data point — against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day, equalling ~1% of baseline. Source: straits.live live tracker, updated 09 NOV 2026 0136Z (sourcing portwatch.imf.org).
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: 1 transit equals ~1% of the ~85/day baseline, far below the 25% threshold (21 transits/day) required to exit the CUT band; the strait remains effectively closed to commercial traffic with ongoing mine strikes and tanker attacks confirmed through November 9, 2026.

dissent.view: UANI reports U.S.-facilitated transits averaged 31.5 vessels/day for November 1-4 (126 transits over 96 hours), which would nominally be ~37% of baseline — but these are explicitly dark/non-AIS vessels escorted by U.S. forces, not standard commercial transits counted by IMF PortWatch.

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan MND (Nov. 8, 2026): 4 PLA sorties, 6 PLAN vessels, 2 official ships detected; 2 sorties entered southwestern ADIZ. Peak activity: 49 sorties on Nov. 3, 32 on Nov. 1, with two Joint Combat Readiness Patrols (JCRPs) conducted Nov. 1 and Nov. 4. ISW/AEI (Nov. 6) assessed PRC may be running a major unannounced exercise simulating Taiwan isolation, coordinating surface forces from Eastern, Northern, and Southern Theater Commands — described as exceeding Justice Mission 2025 in scale. Taiwan NSC (Nov. 3): 100+ PLAN/CCG vessels operating across the region. No blockade declared, no kinetic clash, no named drill announced. Shipping: SCFI/Xeneta rates flat, blank sailings at 4.8%, no Taiwan Strait transit disruption recorded.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Multi-theater PLAN/CCG deployments, 49-sortie spike, and dual JCRPs fit 'large-scale blockade rehearsals and assertive patrols' (Level 1). No actual blockade, kinetic event, or market-corroborated transit disruption rules out Level 2.
taiwan_tension.change_reason: new_event: Nov. 1-6 surge to 49 sorties, two JCRPs in five days, ISW/AEI multi-theater coordination assessment of unannounced isolation-simulation exercise — reinforces Level 1 with stronger evidence than Oct. 26 baseline, but rubric outcome unchanged

dissent.view: Some analysts (bne IntelliNews, Nov. 6) characterise the sustained ring of warships as 'tightening the noose' and rehearsing a 'slow squeeze', implying creeping toward Level 2; however no blockade is in force and no transit has been halted.

export_controls.fact: China MOFCOM on Nov 9 2026 announced a 2-month extension of rare-earth export-control waivers to Jan 10 2027 (Reuters/US News, Nov 9 2026), a de-escalatory move on that specific front. However, China's Oct 16 2026 Announcement No. 48 (40-technology draft controls on AI/chips/solar, interim registration in force, public comment closes Nov 15) and Jul 24 2026 Announcement No. 30 (14 EU entities on Export Control List) and Jun 2026 bans on 10 US companies remain legally in force. On the allied side, NL/EU equipment licensing rules, US annual-licence regime for TSMC/Samsung/SK Hynix China fabs, and the pending MATCH Act pressure on ASML DUV exports remain active. Per CSIS and SIA (Sep 2026 USTR filing), China's April 2026 Decree 834 (Industrial Chain and Supply Chain Security Regulations) also remains in force, granting MOFCOM authorities to impose export controls and trade bans in retaliation for 'discriminatory measures'.
export_controls.rationale: Both sides have active, legally in-force export-control measures enacted or escalated within the trailing 90 days: allied DUV/semiconductor-equipment licensing and entity restrictions (Tightening = 1) plus China's counter-controls on technologies, entities, and materials targeting US/EU firms (Retaliation = 2). The Nov 9 rare-earth waiver extension is a partial de-escalation on one instrument but does not rescind the semiconductor-focused countermeasures; rubric value stays at 2.

dissent.view: Nov 9 rare-earth suspension extension to Jan 10 2027 could be read as bilateral de-escalation reducing effective retaliation pressure, potentially arguing for a downgrade toward 1; Reuters reports it as part of a broader trade-truce extension ahead of APEC Trump-Xi summit

fab_concentration.fact: TSMC 3nm capacity ~180,000 wpm (all Taiwan fabs) by early Q4 2026; 2nm capacity ~90,000 wpm (all five fabs in Taiwan: Hsinchu x2, Kaohsiung x3). Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (N3): equipment installation began Q3 2026, HVM targeted H2 2027 — zero <=3nm wafers produced outside Taiwan. Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm upgrade): HVM 2028. 0% of <=3nm capacity is outside Taiwan as of today. Sources: TrendForce/Economic Daily News Aug 3 2026 (180K 3nm wpm); TechNode/Economic Daily News Aug 5 2026 (~100K 2nm wpm by end-2026, all Taiwan); TSMC Q3 2026 earnings Oct 15 2026 (C.C. Wei); tech-insider.org Nov 2026.
fab_concentration.rationale: With 0% of <=3nm capacity outside Taiwan and no operational overseas leading-edge fab, the rubric condition for EXTREME (value=2) is fully met: <10% outside Taiwan AND no operational overseas leading-edge fab. The 30%-outside-Taiwan figure cited in multiple sources is a future target contingent on Arizona gigafab completion, not current production.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 1 commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz on November 1 2026 (most recent published date), against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day (1.2% of baseline); corroborated by straits.live live tracker updated 09 Nov 2026 2112Z showing 'below a tenth of pre-crisis vessel count'; IRGC struck three tankers near Hormuz on November 9 2026 killing at least 25 sailors; Iran Army Spokesman declared Hormuz stays closed until US accepts 7 conditions (Nov 7 2026). Source: straits.live/report (09 Nov 2026) citing IMF PortWatch; Reuters/multiple outlets via straits.live/briefs/2026-11-06; criticalthreats.org Iran Update 06 Nov 2026.
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Hormuz at 1.2% of baseline is well below the 25% threshold, automatically triggering a CLOSED (2) rating under the rubric regardless of diplomatic statements; Bab el-Mandeb at ~34/day (49% of baseline) with active Houthi attacks and a declared Saudi blockade is CONTESTED (1), but the rubric requires rating the worse chokepoint, so Hormuz controls at 2.

dissent.view: S&P Global Commodities at Sea (via Hellenic Shipping News, Nov 2 2026) reported Hormuz crossings reached a 3-month high in October, suggesting AIS-dark or shadow-fleet tankers inflate actual throughput above PortWatch's AIS-only count

Bab el-Mandeb tanker-only transits (TankerMap AIS, ~8/day tankers as of Nov 6) are severely reduced, though all-vessel counts (Gulf News JMIC, ~34/day) indicate broader commercial traffic remains partially open

cable_incidents.fact: No new submarine cable cut in the Red Sea, Hormuz, or Baltic corridors has been confirmed post-Oct 24, 2026. The dominant load-bearing fact remains the IRGC/Javani public threat to seven Hormuz cables (~Oct 21, 2026, IranIntl/Reuters). APNIC (Oct 14, 2026) confirms Houthi-controlled Red Sea waters 'remain effectively ungovernable for cable protection' and that Sept 2025 Red Sea cuts (SEA-ME-WE 4, IMEWE) have been complicated by Alcatel pausing regional repairs in May 2026 — but no authoritative source confirms a currently-severed, unrepaired major cable in these three corridors as of today. A WACS Atlantic cable is unrepaired today (ITWeb, Nov 9, 2026) but is outside the specified corridors.
cable_incidents.rationale: The rubric scores 1 (THREATENED) because credible official threats to Hormuz cables were made within 90 days (IRGC, ~Oct 21, 2026) and anchor-drag damage on Baltic cables was confirmed in March 2026; however, no source confirms a major cable is severed and unrepaired TODAY in the Red Sea, Hormuz, or Baltic corridors, so the threshold for value 2 (CUT) is not met.

dissent.view: Habtoor Research (Oct 2026) cites India MoEIT reporting that India Europe Xpress, SEA-ME-WE 6, and 2Africa remained under repair as of March 2026 after Sept 2025 Red Sea cuts — if any remain unrepaired today, value could be 2; but no post-Oct 2026 source confirms this.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SIFMA/BNY/Broadridge/DTCC pulse survey (n=340, June 2026, published Sept 22 2026): 86% at least somewhat confident, 13% not confident for cash, 16% for repo; 74% of sell-side firms report tech delays; 88% of delayed buy-side programs cite legal/documentation as dominant constraint; 51% have no formal contingency plan. Additionally, SEC issued a second exemptive relief (Release No. 34-106821, Nov 4 2026) granting SIFMA-requested Rule 15c3-3a Note H relief for broker-dealers on margin collateral delivery for centrally cleared UST transactions. Cash deadline Dec 31 2026 and repo deadline Jun 30 2027 remain unchanged. Sources: SIFMA/DTCC (sifma.org, dtcc.com, Sept 22 2026); SEC.gov Release 34-106821 (Nov 4 2026); Federal Register 2026-22740 (Nov 9 2026).
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: The rubric-defining condition for a 1 is 'documentation backlog, pending exemptive relief, or readiness surveys <60% confident': the Sept 2026 pulse survey shows 13% not confident for cash and persistent legal/tech backlogs, while the Nov 4 2026 15c3-3a Note H exemptive relief resolves one more outstanding item but confirms ongoing implementation friction. No deadline extension or major operational failure (rubric level 2) has occurred, and broad readiness is not yet confirmed (rubric level 0).

dissent.view: DTCC July 2026 GSD Netting Member survey shows 79% already have account setups and nearly 100% are in onboarding pipeline, suggesting cash-clearing readiness is more advanced than the broader SIFMA pulse survey implies

oat_bund.fact: ideal-investisseur.fr (citing Banque de France and Bundesbank data), Nov 5 2026: OAT-Bund 10-year spread = 148.2 bps (OAT 4.75%, Bund 3.27%); corroborated by Armstrong Economics Market Talk Nov 9 2026 intraday quotes (France 4.7450%, Bund 3.2651%) implying ~148.0 bps.
oat_bund.rationale: 148.2 bps = 1.482 percentage points; rubric instructs converting bps to percentage points (divide by 100), giving a value of 1.48. This is a fresh post-Nov-02 reading that is materially lower than the prior 1.63, driven by spread compression in the Nov 3-9 week.
oat_bund.change_reason: new_event: OAT-Bund spread compressed from ~163 bps to ~148 bps in the week of 3-9 Nov 2026, per Banque de France/Bundesbank data via ideal-investisseur.fr (Nov 5) and Armstrong Economics intraday (Nov 9)

dissent.view: cbonds.com reports 10Y France-Germany spread at 154.2 bps as of Nov 5, 2026, ~6 bps wider than the Banque de France/Bundesbank-sourced reading
finimize.com (~Nov 6) reports OAT-Bund spread 'around 154.50 basis points', in line with cbonds but diverging from ideal-investisseur.fr
